newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-PROFILE OF SLALOM WINNER TOMBA.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-PROFILE OF SLALOM WINNER TOMBA.

text.p: Following is a brief profile of Alberto Tomba, the winner of a men's Alpine skiing World Cup slalom on Thursday:

Overall World Cup wins: 48 - slalom: Sestriere (87, 90, 91, 93, 94), Madonna (87, 88, 95), Kranjska Gora (87, 92, 95), Bad Kleinkirchheim (88), Are (88), Oppdal (88), Waterville (89), Geilo (90), Salen (90), Park City (91), Kitzbuehel (92, 95), Wengen (92, 95), Crans Montana (92), Garmisch (93, 94, 95), Stoneham (93), Chamonix (94), Tignes (94), Lech I (94), Lech II (94), Flachau (96), Schladming (97)

Giant slalom: Sestriere (87), Alta Badia (87, 90, 91, 94), Saas Fee (88), Kranjska Gora (90, 95), Lillehammer (91), Aspen (91), Waterville (91), Park City (91), Crans Montana (92), Adelboden (95), Bormio (95)

Other facts - 1987 world championship giant slalom bronze, 1996 world championship slalom and giant slalom gold, 1988 Olympic slalom and giant slalom gold, 1992 Olympic giant slalom gold and slalom silver, 1994 Olympics slalom silver.

The flamboyant Italian had considered retirement after last year's world championships in Sierra Nevada, Spain, but is to participate in his home world championships in Sestriere, starting on Sunday. He had a slow start to the season, missed the opening races due to a knee and wrist injury sustained in a heavy fall during training. Influenza plagued him early this month. Has competed in only four slaloms this season.
